title: SHAP with PySpark MLLib models
question:
I have trained a series of models on Databricks using PySpark Pipelines via MLLib. I want to create SHAP explanations for my output to understand why certain observations are being scored in different ways. However, all my attempts at getting the Python shap package to work with these models have failed. Here's what I've tried.

Suppose I've already trained a pipeline model (mod) on my PySpark dataframes (train and test):

import shap

train_schema = train.schema
train_df = train.toPandas()
test_df = test.toPandas()

I was using shap.KernelExplainer because it accepts a function as input instead of a model and shap does not accept either MLLib models or PySpark dataframes as input. The function converts the data back to spark, does a prediction, then transforms it back to pandas format.

def model_func(df):
  spark_df = spark.createDataFrame(df, schema=train_schema)
  return mod.transform(spark_df).select('prediction').toPandas().values.reshape(-1)

explainer = shap.KernelExplainer(model_func, train_df.iloc[:50,:], link="identity", keep_index=True)

It works up to here. But if I try to create shap values, it throws an attribute error:

shap_values = explainer.shap_values(test_df.iloc[0,:])

I've tried including a masker in the KernelExplainer but I'm really just not sure what the error means.

Is there a way to generate shap explanations on PySpark models?
answer:
Depending if you want to use shap.explainers or explainers from interpret.ext.blackbox.

If you prefer to use shap.KernelExplainer, you can wrap mod.transform(spark_df).select('prediction').toPandas() inside a class. You just need to make sure the class has a predict method and whatever you pass in the KernelExplainers is compatible (i.e pandas dataframe).

class wrapper:
  def __init__(self,columns,model):
    self.cols = cols 
    self.model = model

  def predict(self,args):
     # turning the pandas dataframe back to a pyspark dataframe
     spark_df = spark.createDataFrame(args,self.cols)
     prediction_results = self.model.transform(spark_df)
     output = predictions.select("predictions").toPandas().values.flatten()
     return output 
  
custom_model = wrapper(columns_list,pyspark_model)

# Make sure train_df is a pandas dataframe 
explainer = shap.KernelExplainer(custom_model.predict,
                                 train_df.toPandas())

shap_values = explainer.shap_values(test_df)
global_importance = np.abs(shap_values).mean(0)

You can technically do the same if you wish to use explainers from interpret.ml.blackbox. You can also reference their API documentations

There are two ways of doing it - I will simply show the easier way.

# Assuming you have used mlflow to log an experiment and register the model 
loaded_model =  mlflow.pyfunc.load_model("model_path_goes_here")

class wrapper():
  def __init__(self, model):
    self.model = model
    
  def predict(self, X):
    predictions = self.model.predict(X)
    return np.array([[1-p, p] for p in predictions])

wrapper = wrapper(loaded_model)
explainer = KernelExplainer(
              wrapper,
              initialization_examples = train_df,
              features = train_df.columns.tolist(),
              classes=[0, 1],
              model_task='classification')

explainer.explain_global(train_df.sample(frac=0.002))
explainer.explain_local(test_df)

I am also training models on Databricks using Pyspark pipelines. Although I got these explainers to work, I have yet to figure out a way to pickle these explainers. Regardless, I think you should try making custom model wrappers and see if it works for you as well.
